source.title: A Topological Signature of Learning under Noisy Labels
source.authors: Zhong-Tian Sun; Fan Mo; Prayag Tiwari; Ke-Lin Xia

record.tranche_reason: The study measures predictions on corrupted training-probe examples, which bears on fitting assigned noisy labels, but does not run the original complete-random-label fitting test.
record.gate_note: The study reports that at epoch 50 only 7–11% of corrupted probe examples are predicted as their assigned noisy label, while 71–79% are predicted as their original label. It does not report fitting a completely random labeling to convergence. Persistence measurements and cited prior findings about random-label fitting are not rows.
record.test_reason: Direct predictions on corrupted training examples bear on V4's perfect-fitting component and V6's differential learning of signal and noise. They do not test V1's completely random labeling condition. Persistence trajectories cannot establish label-fitting dynamics.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that noisy supervision produces measurable representation differences, including scale-controlled persistence differences when corrupted-label agreement remains low. They also emphasize pipeline-dependent crossover and stronger average in-sample noise calibration from activation norm than raw persistence.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses symmetric uniform relabelling on a fixed CIFAR-10 training probe and measures prediction agreement alongside representation persistence; it does not reproduce the original complete-random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported label-prediction result is at epoch 50 and covers two partial-noise settings; the study does not report setting-specific prediction fractions.

fits_no_version.finding: Corrupted subsets develop higher persistence, and persistence crossover varies with pipeline and distance construction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy supervision changes representation geometry, including when agreement with corrupted labels remains low.

record.problems: The probe groups are matched in size but not class composition. The setting-specific label-prediction percentages are not reported, and the study does not measure complete random-label fitting to convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No other results directly measure fitting assigned training labels. Persistence values, noise-rate correlations, validation accuracies, and cited prior findings do not report the fitting behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Complete-random-label training accuracy, chance test performance paired with successful fitting, and fitting under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting after longer training and throughout the full corruption range. Reported validation accuracies describe degradation with noise, but are not paired with demonstrated perfect training fit.

Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization preserves true-label generalization. Persistence and averaged test-accuracy comparisons do not establish these.
Direct prediction trajectories establishing when real patterns are acquired and when noisy labels are subsequently memorized; eventual noisy-label memorization.

record.verdict_notes: Selection fraction is not the changed-label fraction because uniform relabelling can redraw the original class. Neither persistence crossover nor cited prior work supplies evidence of successful random-label fitting in this study. The four rows encode two pooled ranges, not four independently reported percentages.

versions.untested_parts: Complete random labeling; zero or near-zero overall training error; test error at chance; unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training; convergence beyond epoch 50.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured whether corrupted training-probe examples were predicted as their assigned noisy label at epoch 50.
rows.measure: Corrupted probe examples predicted as their assigned noisy label
rows.value: 7–11% across the two noise settings; the text does not give the setting-specific value
rows.note: The reported range covers both sf = 0.25 and sf = 0.5; no individual value is assigned to this setting.
rows.check: Remove V1: this is partial corruption, not completely random labeling. Assigned-label agreement is far from perfect at the final epoch. For V6, interpret jointly with original-label agreement; this checkpoint does not establish temporal ordering. The 7–11% range covers both settings and must not be treated as a setting-specific estimate.

source_check.correct: Retain partial for V4. Use cannot_determine for V6: epoch-50 agreement alone cannot establish learning order.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, lines 235–248; Appendix B, symmetric uniform relabelling.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state does not distinguish incomplete fitting under V4 from unmeasured temporal ordering under V6.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10/ResNet-18, symmetric uniform relabelling at selection fractions 0.25 and 0.5, final epoch 50
relationships.reason: R1–R4 show incomplete fitting under this training horizon: only 7–11% of changed-label probe examples match assigned labels, while 71–79% match original labels. Perfect training fit therefore requires qualification by training conditions or duration.
relationships.display_finding: Only 7–11% of changed-label probe examples matched assigned labels, while 71–79% matched original labels.

source_check.reason: R1–R4 establish incomplete assigned-label fitting at epoch 50: 7–11% assigned-label agreement versus 71–79% original-label agreement. This qualifies perfect fitting under the tested training conditions.

relationships.condition: Differential learning of underlying signal and corrupted labels at epoch 50 on the fixed CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 training probe
relationships.reason: R1–R4 show substantially greater original-label agreement (71–79%) than noisy-label agreement (7–11%), consistent with learning shared signal while noise fitting remains low; they do not establish the full temporal sequence.
relationships.display_finding: At epoch 50, original-label agreement was 71–79% versus 7–11% noisy-label agreement, without establishing the full temporal sequence.
